headline: Academic studies show CEO overconfidence contributes to high M&A failure rates
summary: Academic research indicates that between 70% and 90% of corporate acquisitions fail, with CEO overconfidence driving buyers to pay higher prices and select poorer targets.
why: Mergers and acquisitions involve substantial capital allocation; understanding behavioral biases helps institutional investors evaluate governance and corporate strategy risks.

impacts.name: Corporate M&A
impacts.why: Insights into acquisition failure rates highlight strategic risks in corporate dealmaking.
